description: FrontierOne is a creating an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer that blends strategy, space exploration, and AI. Our goal is to let players build and manage a lunar or Martian outpost while learning how astronauts balance power, oxygen, water, food, and radiation protection.
summary:
Spacekeepers is a free browser game that lets children aged 7 to 12 run a Mars outpost and feel the trade-offs real mission planners face. Power is limited, so every new machine competes with the others: the oxygen maker, the greenhouse, the ice mine and the habitat. Soil shelters block radiation, but they cost digging time, a sheltered greenhouse needs more power, and solar panels cannot be sheltered at all. Advice from Mission Control arrives a day late, and a solar flare can block the radio. No choice is free.
GitHub Link: https://github.com/FrontierOneTeam/SpaceExpedition
The space weather is real. Every game day is a real date, and the game shows what NASA's DONKI database recorded on it: solar flares for September 2017 and every day of 2022 to 2024. Two storms are the real ones NASA's Curiosity rover measured on Mars. Other storms follow one labelled game rule tied to real flares. After each period, a report called "This really happened" sets NASA's observations beside what happened in the player's base, and says plainly what is real and what is a simple game model.

It runs on a phone, works offline, and needs no download or account.
Github: https://github.com/FrontierOneTeam/SpaceExpedition
details:
WHAT IT IS

Spacekeepers is a browser game where children aged 7 to 12 run a Mars outpost. The player places buildings and ends the day. Three short chains keep the crew alive: sunlight makes power and power makes air; ice makes water and water grows food; rock makes soil, and soil makes shelter.

THE TRADE-OFFS

- Power: there is never enough for everything. When it runs short, the habitat is served first and the newest machines go dark.

- Radiation shielding: soil shelters protect the crew and machines. Soil must be dug first, a sheltered greenhouse uses more power, and solar panels must stay in the open.

- Life support and food: the crew uses air and food every day, and both depend on power and water.

- Communication delay: Mission Control's advice is always about yesterday, and a big solar flare blocks the radio.

Only three resources sit on screen: power, air and food. No choice is free.

REAL NASA DATA

Every game day is a real date. The game shows NASA's DONKI flare records for 1,110 dates: September 2017 and all of 2022 to 2024. Two storms are real events NASA's Curiosity rover measured on Mars. Other storms follow one labelled game rule tied to real flares. Buildings carry short notes from NASA and Canadian Space Agency pages, including a plant study from the Open Science Data Repository, and the wind is NASA's Perseverance recording. Each period ends with a report, "This really happened", that sets NASA's observations beside the player's base and says what is real and what is simplified. All data is stored in the game with its source. Nothing is fetched while playing, and nothing is called live.

BUILT FOR KIDS

Plain words, with terms like sol and regolith explained on tap. The game never says "game over": it shows why a run ended and offers another try. It works on a phone, offline, with no account.

TOOLS

TypeScript, Vite, Phaser 3, Vitest (300+ automated tests), GitHub Pages.
